name: Russian School of Mathematics
line: RSM teaches a weekly class at the level set for it. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Russian School of Mathematics: RSM teaches a weekly class at one level. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Russian School of Mathematics teaches a weekly live class at a level set for the class, with homework between classes [1][2][5]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. RSM places a child in a class level after an evaluation [2]. Its FAQ says that when homework runs far longer or shorter than half the lesson, the child may be in the wrong level [5].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels, and repeated misses send practice back to what a skill builds on. RSM teaches each grade at three levels, and a class that averages 12 students works at the level set for it [1].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a film where there is one, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In RSM the unit is the weekly class: a live teacher teaches, in person or on video, and homework follows [2][5]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [8].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. In RSM the practice between classes is homework, set to take about half as long as the lesson [5]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in mixed ages and subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [9].

rows.range: Kindergarten through grade 12 in person; grades 2 to 10 online [1][2].
rows.start: An evaluation places the child in one of three class levels for the grade [1][2].
rows.teaching: A live teacher with a class averaging 12 students, each week, then homework of about half the lesson's length [1][5].
rows.next: The class's lessons for its level. If homework runs far longer or shorter than expected, the FAQ says the level may be wrong [5].
rows.mastery: None found in the pages we read [1][4].
rows.review: None found in the pages we read [1][4].
rows.adult: Gets the child to class, in person or online, each week, and sees that homework gets done [5].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found. No entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [6][7].

theirs: Russian School of Mathematics, known as RSM, is an after-school math program for kindergarten through grade 12 [1][4]. Classes began in 1997 [3]. RSM describes its programs as one continuous curriculum [1], and frames its approach as a classical tradition of using math to develop the mind [4].

An evaluation matches a child to a class level [2]. Each grade has three levels, and classes average 12 students [1]. A class meets each week with a live teacher, in person or on video, for 1.5 to 4 hours a week online depending on grade [2][5]. Homework follows each class and should take about half as long as the lesson [5].
credit: A live teacher in a small class. A learner can ask a person and hear an answer in the moment [1].
A Competition program for students drawn to contest math [1][4].

theirs: We found no outcome study of RSM on its site. It has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse as of November 2026 [6][7].
RSM reports contest results for its students who entered, such as the AMC 8 and HMMT [1]. These count only students who chose to take part, with no comparison group.
ours: The two findings that bear most on this comparison: worked examples improve math performance across 55 studies [8], and across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in mixed ages and subjects, with smaller effects in primary and high school, feedback that explains averaged 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [9]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and the code is public.

them: Your child learns best with a live teacher and classmates, in a weekly class.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want every answer checked and followed by the worked steps.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Russian School of Mathematics?
questions.answer: RSM places a child in a class level and teaches a weekly live class, with homework between classes [2][5]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Russian School of Mathematics work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study on its site. It has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse as of November 2026 [6][7]. RSM reports contest results for students who chose to enter, with no comparison group [1].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
